headline: A top official of the International Monetary Fund said new rules on advanced AI may be needed, with cyber attacks the leading risk.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 because only the paywalled article's preview paragraph could be read; it is a possibility, not a proposal.
importance_line: What changed: a senior IMF official was reported as saying new AI rules may be needed, with cyber risk named as the leading concern, which affects the public and organisations facing cyber attacks first, then regulators, then AI developers, and the doubt is that he said rules "may be needed", not that any are planned.
summary: MLex reports that Dan Katz, the International Monetary Fund's first deputy managing director, said new AI rules may be needed to hold back the development of the most advanced AI tools, which he says pose risks to society, and named cybersecurity as the leading risk.
notes: MLex is paywalled; the summary rests on the public preview paragraph only (headline plus the opening lines), not the full article. The date and place of Katz's remarks are not stated.
